clue.text: Way to overcome an Afghan?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of, and so overcomes, the second

parts.note: a way or track is a path
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of which route will defeat a man from Afghanistan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reuses 'an' from the wordplay only in the surface; the defining word is 'Afghan'. 'to overcome' places PATH above AN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathans, also called Pashtuns, are an ethnic people of Afghanistan and Pakistan.

clue.text: Encourage to voice intuition

indicators.note: to voice something is to say it out loud, so the word for intuition is spoken

parts.note: intuition is insight, an instinctive understanding

explanation.surface: Urging someone to speak up about their gut feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge or stir someone on, which is to encourage them.

clue.text: Full-length internal course supplied with food and drink at various stages

definitions.text: Full-length internal course supplied with food and drink at various stages

parts.words: Full-length internal course supplied with food and drink at various stages
parts.note: reads like a residential training course with meals laid on, but describes the body's digestive tract running from mouth to anus

explanation.surface: A complete in-house training programme, catered throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a programme of study and 'internal' an in-house one; in fact the course is a passage inside the body that food passes along.
explanation.definitionFit: The digestive passage runs the full length of the body's trunk and receives food and drink in turn along its stages.

clue.text: Fully support, but fail to intervene

definitions.meaning: to remain loyal and back them

explanation.surface: Someone who backs a friend completely but won't step in when needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both staying loyal to a person and looking on passively while something happens.

clue.text: Fortune seekers threaten usurers with violence

indicators.note: violence wrecks things, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: People after money menace moneylenders by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with violence' rearranges THREATEN and USURERS together, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure hunters search for buried riches, which makes them seekers of fortune.

clue.text: Old newspapers, frequently out of date

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
The Times is another British newspaper

explanation.surface: Back issues of the press often become stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newspapers' gives two papers at once: FT (the Financial Times) and TIMES. 'out of date' marks the answer as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old-fashioned literary way of saying often.

clue.text: Eliminate being angry when dismissed

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry
a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: Someone getting cross after being sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman dismissed is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike a word through on a page is to delete or remove it.

clue.text: Offhand challenge that may be thrown

definitions.text: Offhand challenge that may be thrown

parts.words: Offhand challenge that may be thrown
parts.note: offhand reads as casual, but means a glove pulled off the hand and flung down as a dare to fight

explanation.surface: A casual dare that might be tossed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offhand' seems to mean casual; read as off-hand, it is a glove removed from the hand. Throwing one down was the knight's way of issuing a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured glove thrown to the ground was the traditional challenge to combat.

clue.text: Put right former abuse

indicators.note: to abuse something is to misuse or mistreat it, so these letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Correcting a past mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abuse' rearranges FORMER.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something is to correct or improve it.

clue.text: Answer all of us dread

parts.note: all of us together is we

explanation.surface: Everyone fears the reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential fear, so it is a kind of dread.

clue.text: But he may run a standing committee

definitions.text: But he may run a standing committee

parts.words: But he may run a standing committee
parts.note: a standing committee is a permanent one, but the person leading it sits in a seat, so the joke is that he never stands

explanation.surface: A remark about who leads a permanent committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing committee' means a permanent body; 'But' points at the joke that its leader takes a seat rather than standing.
explanation.definitionFit: The person presiding over a committee meeting is the one who runs it.

clue.text: Swear one's watching cricket

parts.note: someone watching a match is at it
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A spectator at the cricket takes an oath.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, so a spectator is 'at Test'.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare something true under oath.

clue.text: Extremely unusual for Cynthia to look sad

definitions.text: Extremely unusual for Cynthia to look sad

parts.words: Extremely unusual for Cynthia to look sad
parts.note: Cynthia is a poetic name for the moon goddess, and to look sad is to look blue, so a melancholy moon is a rare sight

explanation.surface: It is rare for a woman called Cynthia to seem downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Cynthia is a name of Artemis, goddess of the moon, and 'sad' is blue: a blue moon is proverbially rare.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hardly ever, describing something that happens very rarely.

clue.text: Record in advance either half of chorus-girl routine

definitions.meaning: to film or record it ready for later
the high-kicking chorus line dance is two identical halves

explanation.surface: Pre-recording a dancing troupe's act.
explanation.walkthrough: The chorus-girl routine is the cancan, a French high-kicking dance.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pre-record or preserve; it is also each half of the cancan dance name.

clue.text: Leave a caramel eventually to solidify

parts.note: congé is permission to leave, or a dismissal
taken as written

indicators.note: eventually points to how the word caramel ends, its final letter

explanation.surface: Leaving toffee to set hard.
explanation.walkthrough: CONGE (French congé) is formal leave or dismissal; 'eventually' takes L, the last letter of 'caramel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to thicken and set, which is to become solid.

clue.text: Like a word about the future of Delphi, for example

definitions.text: Like a word about the future of Delphi, for example

parts.words: Like a word about the future of Delphi, for example
parts.note: the priestess at Delphi in ancient Greece gave prophecies, so this describes the style of such a pronouncement

explanation.surface: A remark about what lies ahead for the Greek site of Delphi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Delphi' looks like it belongs to 'the future'; it qualifies the 'word', the prophecy given at Delphi in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes prophetic or cryptic statements such as those given at shrines in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Immature, surreptitious garden pest

parts.note: green means inexperienced or immature
fly is slang for sly or crafty

explanation.surface: A young, sneaky creature in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: These small sap-sucking aphids damage garden plants.

clue.text: Studies something with unknown thickness

parts.note: dens are private studies or rooms
it stands for an unspecified thing
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Researching something mysterious and its bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studies' reads as a verb but is a noun, rooms for working: DENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Density is how closely packed a substance is, its compactness or thickness.

clue.text: Anger that I had to join soldiers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Fury that drove me to enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had to join' is a link joining I to RE, the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is wrath or fury.

clue.text: Miserable, unlike a little friend of snow white?

definitions.text: unlike a little friend of snow white?
definitions.meaning: one of the seven dwarfs in the Snow White tale is called Happy, so to be unlike him is to be not Happy

explanation.surface: A sad person who doesn't resemble one of the seven dwarfs.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: Happy is one of Snow White's dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sad or wretched is the opposite of the cheerful dwarf, the dwarf's name with 'un-' in front.

clue.text: Book of bible offers salvation — so does being in mass?

definitions.meaning: Numbers is a book of the Old Testament, and salvation is safety, which that book holds
being part of a crowd also keeps one safe, as the proverb says

explanation.surface: Scripture offers deliverance, and so might attending church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' suggests a church service but means a crowd. The first part reads the phrase literally: safety can be found in the Book of Numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a group gives protection that a lone individual lacks.

clue.text: British control frontier

parts.note: order means control or discipline

explanation.surface: Britain regulates its frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the boundary line between countries.

clue.text: Enjoy contents of barrel? I shall

indicators.note: contents are what lies inside, so the letters are found within these words

explanation.surface: Asking whether to drink what's in the cask, and agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of' takes the letters inside 'barrel? I shall'.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to take great pleasure in it.

clue.text: Old coin from Africa

definitions.meaning: a pre-decimal British gold coin worth twenty-one shillings
a country of West Africa, standing for the continent as an example

explanation.surface: A piece of antique money originating in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The coin was named after the West African region whose gold it was first struck from. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both an old British coin worth 21 shillings and a West African country.

clue.text: Absolutely last, in any case

definitions.meaning: later than every other thing, at the very end
used to mean nevertheless or anyway

explanation.surface: Something final, whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both following everything else and anyway or nonetheless.

clue.text: Tot of whisky for nastiness of cold

definitions.meaning: the biting sharpness of chilly air

explanation.surface: A dram to fight off the chill.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a small drink of spirits and the sharp sting of frosty air.

clue.text: All made sick with pea and rice dish

indicators.note: being made sick upsets the system, so these letters are churned up

explanation.surface: A whole group falls ill from eating peas and rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made sick' rearranges ALL and PEA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish dish of saffron rice cooked with seafood or meat.

clue.text: Each poem is wayward

parts.note: per means for each, as in a pound per head
a verse is a poem or piece of poetry

explanation.surface: Every line of poetry is wilful.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means contrary and stubbornly unreasonable, like someone wayward.
